docs.text: What the guarantees mean ¶ A certificate tells you what the evidence supports. It does not tell you how difficult a model will find the puzzle. The pipeline in three stages ¶ 1. Create and transform a case ¶ Validate the configuration, sample a seeded world, and build truthful core reports. Then apply the requested changes: irrelevant records, redundancy, false reports or presentation changes. 2. Certify what can be inferred ¶ Check the evidence under its public reliability rule. Create agent partitions, verify coalition conditions, and screen selected structural duplicates and splits. 3. Export and evaluate ¶ Render deterministic text and write a streamed bundle. Export only public agent views, then score returned actions against evaluator-only answers. What a score means ¶ Outcome The question it answers Correct Did the agent name the actual responsible suspect? Supported Does the available evidence justify that answer? Sufficient evidence Could this view identify one responsible suspect? Valid protocol Did the agent return a permitted final action? Abstained Did it choose not to name a suspect? A correct guess on ambiguous evidence can be unsupported . Abstaining when several suspects remain possible can be appropriate; abstaining when one answer is established is unnecessary. Four different evidence states ¶ Unique: the evidence permits exactly one responsible suspect. Ambiguous: it permits several. Inconsistent: it permits none. Unresolved: the solver ran out of time or work before establishing the result. Unresolved is never treated as a proof of uniqueness, inconsistency or unsatisfiability. A private view can be ambiguous even when the complete view is unique. Globally ambiguous data remains ambiguous even with all reports. One culprit does not mean one complete world ¶ Suspects can share motives, rooms, weapons or times. The default repeated assignment mode permits this. Finding one responsible suspect does not determine every unmentioned attribute. You might rule out Ada without learning which weapon she has. The distinct mode instead forbids repeated values within an attribute. It needs enough active domain values for every suspect. What does “at most k false reports” mean? ¶ A truthful clue describes the sampled world. A report is the statement the agent receives; a sampled corruption can make it false. An allowance of at most two permits zero, one or two false reports. It does not assert that exactly two are false. The evaluator keeps the actual corrupted identities and count private. Structural rules stay trusted, including the rule connecting crime attributes to the culprit. Extra evidence is not one intervention ¶ Change What it adds or changes Independent nuisance records Satisfiable claims about disjoint variables. They cannot change the target candidates. Core-entailed additions Facts already implied by the useful core. They can add redundancy. Connected decoys Entailed relational additions involving target variables. False reports Statements that change the reliability problem. Prose padding Presentation text without additional factual claims. Do not treat these as interchangeable ways to make a puzzle harder. Necessary reports are not a difficulty score ¶ The total report count is different from the minimum sufficient subset : the fewest original reports needed to force an answer under the reliability rule. A lower bound is not an exact minimum until it matches an upper bound. Neither count certifies proof depth, model accuracy or strategic diversity. Simple construction heuristics can solve some high-burden families. The production and independent Boolean encodings agree, but both use CP-SAT. Tiny exhaustive reference enumeration provides an engine-independent check. Evidence sharing has limits ¶ Coalition checks currently support up to eight agents and can be expensive. Replicated or forwarded reports retain their original identities. The current bounded forwarding protocol is programmed. It is not evidence of learned dialogue, communication emergence or an optimal sharing policy. Seeds, splits and duplicate screening ¶ World-hash allocation keeps paired variants in the same split . Configured holdout families go to the transfer split. Screening checks selected structural fingerprints and renamings. It does not detect every equivalent strategy or reasoning shortcut. A family holdout alone does not prove out-of-distribution competence. Rendering, labels and default domains English comes from deterministic templates, not an LLM. Internal suspect IDs are S01 , S02 , and so on. The naming_seed permutes the Person/Entity display labels. Default domain values are: Weapon: Rope, Wrench, Poison, Knife. Location: Study, Kitchen, Library, Garden. Motive: Revenge, Inheritance, Jealousy, Blackmail. Time: 20:00, 21:00, 22:00, 23:00. Customize puzzle.config.domains with distinct, nonempty strings. The formatter JSON-escapes quotes and Unicode. Inspect the resolved configuration before running a study.

docs.text: Four research recipes ¶ Start with a concrete question, generate a small example, then inspect the guarantees before evaluating a model. All commands on this page run offline. Use a new output directory for each example. 1. Add irrelevant evidence ¶ Question: can more irrelevant evidence improve supported accuracy? clue-benchmark generate-dataset \ --preset noise-volume \ --output runs/noise This preset creates: One branching world with four necessary reports . 100 satisfiable, independent records unrelated to the target answer. Complete evidence for one agent, with useful reports first. No false reports. The original pilot suggested an improvement for Lite. The follow-up did not repeat that benefit consistently: the primary score was 10/12 at both endpoint doses , while costs rose sharply. See all doses, phases and limitations → Replay the saved measurements: clue-benchmark examples replay nuisance-followup \ --output runs/noise-results Prepare a separate matched study without running it Supply explicit reviewed model prices and the prior measured bank: clue-benchmark prepare-nuisance-followup \ --models models.json \ --prior-bank prior/bank \ --output runs/new-followup Preparation creates candidates and maximum reservations. It does not authorize inference . The completed October 27 allowance is closed at an estimated $6.96 of $10.00 , with no holds. Recognizable records are different from adversarial prose. Changing context length and composition together does not isolate a reasoning mechanism. Any new paid study needs a separate plan and budget. 2. Split and share evidence ¶ Question: does the receiver have enough information to answer? clue-benchmark generate-dataset \ --preset distributed \ --output runs/distributed The complete view is unique, while private views are ambiguous. Forwarding retains the original report identities. The saved star-forwarding success applies to a particular protocol and fixture. It is not a universal ranking of network topologies or learned communication. Work through the eight-world replay → 3. Introduce false reports ¶ Question: can an agent reason under a public at-most-k reliability rule? clue-benchmark generate-dataset \ --preset false-reports \ --output runs/false Inspect the resolved configuration: clue-benchmark explain-config --preset false-reports This preset publishes an allowance of at most two false reports , with one sampled false report . The actual corrupted identities remain evaluator-only. The answer is certified under the public rule. A historical fixed-allowance experiment scored Lite 8/8, 7/8, 8/8 at 0/1/2 actual corruptions; Flash scored 8/8 throughout. Necessary evidence was not held fixed, so these small results do not establish a monotonic difficulty effect. Understand the reliability rule → 4. Explore evidence burden ¶ Question: does the amount of necessary evidence predict difficulty? clue-benchmark generate-dataset \ --preset hard-example \ --output runs/hard This small example has eight suspects and eight necessary reports . It is not the measured large hard regime. Historical results show why that distinction matters: At 32 necessary reports , Flash scored 30/30 in each of two path/tree arms; Lite scored 9/30 and 7/30. Some constructions also admit simple heuristics. A fresh 48-world hard confirmation produced 9 correct, 28 wrong and 11 abstentions under a specified output budget. An adaptive six-world comparison improved from 2/6 to 5/6 with more output allowance. Report structure, model resources and study design all affect interpretation. Do not merge these settings into one score. Read the hard-case and resource results →

Keep historical checkouts and budgets separate. The closed follow-up completed 146 paid requests : 144 scored assignments and two probes. Estimated spend is $6.96 , holds $0.00 , against a $10.00 cap. Do not reuse that allowance or launch child plans independently. 2. Verify the candidate ¶ Retain logs and hashes for: Offline tests and parameter coverage. Strict documentation build. Wheel/source-archive build and metadata checks. Review distribution copies ¶ Scan source, history and downloadable archives for credentials, authorizations, ledgers, checkpoints, personal data and local paths. docs.text: CLI and Python reference ¶ Find the command you need, then open the advanced evaluation details only when you need them. Find a preset ¶ clue-benchmark presets list clue-benchmark presets show quickstart clue-benchmark --help lists every installed command. clue-benchmark --version prints the software version. Generate and inspect ¶ Generate with one configuration source: --preset NAME or --config PATH . clue-benchmark generate-dataset \ --preset quickstart \ --output runs/demo Command Purpose explain-config --preset quickstart Show resolved values and field descriptions. profile-dataset --preset quickstart Profile a declared generation configuration. validate-dataset runs/demo Check the bundle and independent semantics. inspect-case runs/demo --agent 0 Show one agent's public evidence. --output and --workers override values from the selected preset or configuration file. explain-config accepts the same selectors and overrides. Use --case-id ID to inspect a specific case. Export public evidence ¶ clue-benchmark export-public runs/demo \ --agent 0 \ --output runs/agent.jsonl Only allowlisted public case/report fields are exported. Give the agent this file, not the evaluator bundle. Replay a saved example ¶ clue-benchmark examples replay nuisance-followup \ --output runs/nuisance Example name What it recomputes distributed-evidence Solver information controls on historical worlds. nuisance-followup Initial, extension and exploratory combined measured results. measured-results All packaged historical panels with separate study/settings identities. These commands make no model calls . The nuisance and measured-results replays accept --figures when the optional figures extra is installed. Build a readable report ¶ clue-benchmark report runs/sample-score.json \ --output runs/sample-report Open runs/sample-report/index.html . Reports include escaped text, exact source JSON and machine-readable output. They never run inference. Use Python ¶ from clue_benchmark import ( evaluate_agent, export_public, generate_dataset, inspect_case, resolve_config, validate_dataset, ) config = resolve_config( name="quickstart", output="runs/python-demo", ) generate_dataset(config) validate_dataset("runs/python-demo") export_public( "runs/python-demo", "runs/python-agent.jsonl", agent_id=0, ) public_case = inspect_case("runs/python-demo", agent_id=0) print(public_case["rules"]) result = evaluate_agent( "runs/python-demo", lambda view: {"kind": "abstain"}, ) Also available: CommunityConfig , generate_case , partition , score , profile_dataset and iter_cases . The latter streams public bundle rows. A public view is not process isolation evaluate_agent supplies copies of public fields to a trusted callable; the evaluator still owns the labels. Run untrusted code in a separate process with exported public files, then score its returned actions in the evaluator process. Supported final actions ¶ Name a listed internal suspect ID , not its display name: {"kind": "answer", "target": "S01"} Or abstain: {"kind": "abstain"} Native tools are answer(target) and abstain() . Missing, malformed or extra actions count as protocol failures , separately from wrong answers on sufficient evidence. Paid evaluation: preparation and execution ¶ Preparation and dry runs work without provider credentials. Actual execution is separately authorized. Prepare an evaluation plan clue-benchmark prepare-community-evaluation runs/demo \ --models models.json \ --output plan.json \ --ceiling-microdollars 1000000 The example ceiling is $1.00 . Preparation freezes explicit models, prices and settings; it does not spend or authorize that amount. Defaults: Conditions: complete, independent private views and sharing. Graph: complete; other choices are star, ring and chain. Sharing: three rounds, at most 64 reports per message. Repeats: one. Input format: structured_text . --input-view text_only omits formal constraints. Keep those results separate from structured-text results. Each model record supplies id , vendor , model , settings , context_tokens , input_microdollars_per_million_tokens and output_microdollars_per_million_tokens . An optional identity is an exact expected returned model string; tokenizer_identity is descriptive. Vendor-specific settings are validated. Billed output allowances include thinking where applicable. One dollar equals 1,000,000 microdollars . Serialized-byte bounds include tool overhead. Context overflow is rejected, never truncated. Dry-run, execution and durable budget controls clue-benchmark run-community-evaluation plan.json \ --dataset runs/demo \ --output runs/evaluation \ --dry-run Actual execution needs --execute --authorization human.json with a human, plan-bound contract. The command never creates approval. Request timeout: 600 seconds . Automatic retries: zero . Persistent SQLite reservations survive interruptions and concurrent launches. Settled usage plus unresolved maximum reservations must fit the plan cap. Unknown usage or identity/resource breaches stop execution and retain a conservative hold. Do not edit ledger balances or assume unresolved calls were free. The completed $10.00 follow-up used one shared allowance across child plans and probes; a separate cap per arm was not allowed. Files, errors and concurrent runs ¶ Success summaries: JSON on stdout. Invalid or incomplete work: exit status 2 with an actionable error on stderr. Exports, reports and replays: refuse an existing destination. Generation: resumes only a matching source/config checkpoint. Complete matching datasets return without being regenerated or rewritten. Frozen evaluations: reject source/config drift. Atomic writes and concurrency guarantees in 0.5.0rc2 Generation and native evaluation take exclusive per-directory locks on Linux and macOS. Simultaneous writers receive a short error. A request that loses an atomic budget reservation is never dispatched. Ledger identity creation is serialized. Unknown usage still stops execution and holds the maximum. JSON writes use unique temporary files and atomic publication. Public exports and new evaluator outputs do not overwrite existing files. An occupied evaluator output is rejected before calling the agent. Reports validate their source before creating output, escape text, retain exact JSON, and keep phase tables keyboard-scrollable. Advanced reproduction and legacy commands ¶ Prepare, run or analyze the original follow-up protocol prepare-nuisance-followup prepares matched inputs and maximum costs offline. It grants no execution permit. clue-benchmark run-nuisance-followup runs/followup This preflights the original frozen study offline. Explicit execution requires --execute --authorization human.json . It serializes the study, checks child ceilings, and stops later jobs after unknown usage or a failed compatibility probe. Fixed child ledgers prevent replay on resume. The original manifest binds 96 scored slots plus at most two probes. The final expansion is recorded separately; the closed allowance cannot be reused. clue-benchmark analyze-nuisance-followup runs/followup \ --output runs/followup-analysis Analysis preserves never-dispatched slots. Incomplete panel accuracy and paired effects remain null until completion. Completed analyses use world-level attempt means, descriptive cluster bootstrap, exact sign-flip analysis and between-model differences. No model is called. Unpack an explicit reproduction archive clue-benchmark unpack-archive study.tar.gz \ --sha256 PUBLISHED_HASH \ --output runs/unpacked Use the actual published hash, not the placeholder above. The command verifies it before extraction and rejects links, traversal and duplicate paths. The default uncompressed limit is one billion bytes; override with --maximum-bytes . Full study archives are separate from the public sanitized outcome downloads and remain pending review where not released. Legacy v0.3 interfaces Flat generate , validate , export , the legacy Config API and v0.3 archives retain their original shapes. They are separate from community bundles. Old investigation/request-clue interfaces are historical. Current conditions are complete evidence, independent private views and bounded forwarding.

docs.text: Find a generation setting ¶ Start with a preset. Change a small number of settings, then inspect the resolved configuration before generating data. clue-benchmark explain-config --preset quickstart Common starting points: construction family , number of suspects , irrelevant records , false reports , agents , seed and workers . Search by name or description below. Open a setting to see its type, default and compatibility rules. With JavaScript disabled, every entry remains readable. These controls affect local generation and certification. None authorizes paid inference. Examples are JSON values to place at the named path. Defaults come from the current dataclasses; coverage is tested. Evaluation controls and troubleshooting are separate. puzzle.family ¶ Type: string · Default / JSON example: "standard" Construction family: standard, pairwise, cross_attribute, equality_tree, branching, redundant_paths. Family-specific enabled types must remain available. A family is not a difficulty guarantee. puzzle.assignment_mode ¶ Type: string · Default / JSON example: "repeated" repeated permits shared attribute values; distinct requires at least suspect_count active values in every domain and forbids equality families. puzzle.extra_clue_scope ¶ Type: string · Default / JSON example: "all" all samples from all attributes; non_target_attributes requires branching/equality_tree and at least two attributes. puzzle.attribute_mismatches ¶ Type: int | None · Default / JSON example: null Optional integer 1..number of attributes; only redundant_paths. Controls how many attribute anchors differ from the culprit. puzzle.config.suspect_count ¶ Type: integer · Default / JSON example: 4 Integer 2..64 suspects. More suspects increase encoding size and subset search; no universal accuracy prediction. puzzle.config.domains ¶ Type: object Default / JSON example: { "location": [ "Study", "Kitchen", "Library", "Garden" ], "motive": [ "Revenge", "Inheritance", "Jealousy", "Blackmail" ], "time": [ "20:00", "21:00", "22:00", "23:00" ], "weapon": [ "Rope", "Wrench", "Poison", "Knife" ] } Map of 1..8 nonempty attribute names to 2..32 distinct strings. Domains may contain unicode/quotes. Changing values changes the world identity. Default lists are printed in the resolved configuration. puzzle.config.clue_count ¶ Type: integer · Default / JSON example: 8 Positive integer core reports, before evidence transformations. Must cover all configured minima. Equality constructions require at least suspect_count; redundant_paths requires (suspect_count+1)*attributes. puzzle.config.enabled_types ¶ Type: array Default / JSON example: [ "crime_different_from", "crime_negative", "crime_positive", "crime_same_as", "indirect_negative", "indirect_positive", "suspect_different_from", "suspect_same_as", "unary_negative", "unary_positive" ] Nonempty unique list of the ten supported clue predicates. Constructed families require their named predicates; see predicate reference. puzzle.config.alpha ¶ Type: number · Default / JSON example: 0.7 Sampling weight/control in [0,1]. Direct category weight alpha; indirect category weight 1-alpha. Construction also uses alpha when choosing available direct versus relational anchors. Rejection and availability condition these weights. puzzle.config.beta ¶ Type: number · Default / JSON example: 0.75 Conditional positive relationship weight in [0,1] within indirect sampling, with complement for negative relationships. Availability and rejection alter realized frequencies; not a measured difficulty slider. puzzle.config.min_murderer_links ¶ Type: integer · Default / JSON example: 1 Nonnegative integer lower bound on murderer-link reports, at most clue_count. Hard accepted-case filter. puzzle.config.max_murderer_links ¶ Type: int | None · Default / JSON example: null Optional nonnegative integer upper bound, no smaller than the minimum. Impossible limits exhaust candidates. puzzle.config.max_positive_murderer_links ¶ Type: int | None · Default / JSON example: null Optional nonnegative cap on positive murderer links; may conflict with available family anchors. puzzle.config.min_indirect_clues ¶ Type: integer · Default / JSON example: 0 Nonnegative minimum number of indirect reports, at most clue_count. Requires enabled indirect types. puzzle.config.min_unique_subset_size ¶ Type: integer · Default / JSON example: 1 Positive minimum sufficient subset size, at most clue_count. Community sufficient bounds cannot undercut this legacy minimum. puzzle.config.require_indirect_essential ¶ Type: boolean · Default / JSON example: false Boolean hard requirement: at least one indirect clue is essential; impossible with no indirect types. puzzle.config.min_pairwise_clues ¶ Type: integer · Default / JSON example: 0 Nonnegative required suspect-comparison count, at most clue_count. May reject unsupported families. puzzle.config.active_values_per_attribute ¶ Type: int | None · Default / JSON example: null Optional integer 2..smallest domain size. Distinct assignment also requires at least suspect_count active values. puzzle.config.reasoning_route ¶ Type: string · Default / JSON example: "standard" standard, pairwise or cross_attribute legacy construction route. Keep standard for equality constructions; family and route must agree. puzzle.config.max_attempts ¶ Type: integer · Default / JSON example: 64 Positive bounded legacy construction attempts per candidate; increasing it costs solver time and does not relax semantic filters. puzzle.config.mutation_steps ¶ Type: integer · Default / JSON example: 12 Nonnegative legacy search mutation steps. Zero skips mutation; it does not skip certification. puzzle.config.max_solver_calls ¶ Type: integer · Default / JSON example: 10000 Positive maximum legacy solver calls. Exhaustion means unresolved, never a proof. puzzle.config.solver_seconds ¶ Type: number · Default / JSON example: 2.0 Positive per-solve wall-time seconds in legacy construction. Timeouts mean unresolved. puzzle.config.solver_work ¶ Type: number · Default / JSON example: 0.2 Positive CP-SAT deterministic work bound. Engine-specific effort units; unrelated to model reasoning depth. puzzle.config.generation_seconds ¶ Type: number · Default / JSON example: 30.0 Positive total legacy generation wall-time seconds. Independent of community certification_seconds. evidence.minimum_sufficient_clues ¶ Type: int | None · Default / JSON example: null Optional nonnegative certified lower bound in reports. Must not exceed maximum or undercut legacy minimum; ambiguous cases forbid it. evidence.maximum_sufficient_clues ¶ Type: int | None · Default / JSON example: null Optional nonnegative certified upper bound in reports; ambiguous cases forbid a sufficient subset. evidence.entailed_clues ¶ Type: integer · Default / JSON example: 0 Nonnegative count of extra core-entailed reports. Can improve redundancy and model performance; increases text and certification cost. evidence.connected_decoys ¶ Type: integer · Default / JSON example: 0 Nonnegative count of extra relational entailed reports connected to target variables. Different from independent nuisance. evidence.irrelevant_records ¶ Type: integer · Default / JSON example: 0 Nonnegative count of satisfiable independent one-variable components, appended by default. Above 1000 requires large_corpus=true. Increases export and model input cost. evidence.false_reports ¶ Type: integer · Default / JSON example: 0 Integer 0..2 actual sampled corruptions; private evaluator information. Cannot exceed corruption_allowance. evidence.corruption_allowance ¶ Type: int | None · Default / JSON example: 0 Optional integer 0..2 public at-most-k rule; resolves to false_reports when omitted. At most is not exactly k. evidence.answerability ¶ Type: string · Default / JSON example: "unique" unique or ambiguous after all reports and the reliability rule. Ambiguous requires null sufficient bounds and null minimum coalition size. evidence.corruption_strategy ¶ Type: string · Default / JSON example: "random" random or targeted. Targeted false reports require unique answerability and may increase solver search. evidence.corruption_search_attempts ¶ Type: integer · Default / JSON example: 12 Positive targeted-search attempt cap. Exhaustion retains rejection evidence; never implies success. evidence.maximum_alternative_margin ¶ Type: int | None · Default / JSON example: null Optional positive maximum alternative reliability margin; requires unique answerability. Extra solver profiling cost. distribution.agent_count ¶ Type: integer · Default / JSON example: 2 Integer 1..8. Explicitly use one for single-agent work; default two. Coalition enumeration grows exponentially. distribution.shared_reports ¶ Type: integer · Default / JSON example: 0 Nonnegative count visible to every agent, no larger than total report count. distribution.private_replication ¶ Type: integer · Default / JSON example: 1 Integer 1..max(1,agent_count-1) owners per non-shared report; repeated presentation retains original report identity. distribution.per_agent_quotas ¶ Type: list[int] | None · Default / JSON example: null Optional exact nonnegative report counts, one per agent. Must be feasible with sharing and replication; impossible quotas reject candidates. distribution.minimum_coalition_size ¶ Type: int | None · Default / JSON example: 2 Optional integer 1..agent_count. Hard certified minimum team size; null for globally ambiguous data. distribution.max_attempts ¶ Type: integer · Default / JSON example: 128 Positive bounded partition-search retries; more retries cost certification time, not a relaxed quota. presentation.theme ¶ Type: string · Default / JSON example: "mystery" mystery or investigation. Uses Person/Entity labels, deterministic wording and no LLM. presentation.naming_seed ¶ Type: integer · Default / JSON example: 0 Integer seed for label permutation, independent of the sampled world; labels are not real people. presentation.template ¶ Type: string · Default / JSON example: "compact" compact or expanded deterministic report wording. Expanded adds a fixed sentence to each report. presentation.clue_order ¶ Type: string · Default / JSON example: "shuffle" shuffle, canonical or reverse. docs.text: How to read a clue ¶ Each report has a readable sentence and a formal constraint. This page pairs each active clue type with a true example and a counterexample. Reading the notation ¶ x(s, a) means suspect s has a value for attribute a . c means the responsible suspect. Crime values equal x(c, a) . Examples use suspects A and B , colors red/blue and rooms hall/study. Unmentioned attributes can take any permitted values. Reports may be false only under the public at-most-k rule. Structural rules stay trusted. Values may repeat unless distinct assignment is explicitly required. A suspect has a value ¶ Type: unary_positive . Suspect "A" has "color" = "red". Formal: x(A, color) = red . True example: A is red. Counterexample: A is blue. A suspect does not have a value ¶ Type: unary_negative . Suspect "A" has "color" != "red". Formal: x(A, color) ≠ red . True example: A is blue. Counterexample: A is red. The culprit has a value ¶ Type: crime_positive . The murderer has "color" = "red". Formal: x(c, color) = red . True example: culprit A is red. Counterexample: culprit A is blue. The culprit does not have a value ¶ Type: crime_negative . The murderer has "color" != "red". Formal: x(c, color) ≠ red . True example: culprit A is blue. Counterexample: culprit A is red. The sampling code categorizes this as indirect. That internal category can differ from everyday language. The culprit shares a suspect's value ¶ Type: crime_same_as . The murderer has the same "color" value as suspect "A". Formal: x(c, color) = x(A, color) . True example: culprit B is blue and A is blue. Counterexample: culprit B is red and A is blue. This does not assert that A is responsible. Different suspects can share a value. The culprit differs from a suspect ¶ Type: crime_different_from . The murderer has a different "color" value as suspect "A". Formal: x(c, color) ≠ x(A, color) . True example: culprit B is red and A is blue. Counterexample: culprit B is blue and A is blue. If A is responsible, this report is always false. Two suspects share a value ¶ Type: suspect_same_as . Suspects "A" and "B" have the same "color" values. Formal: x(A, color) = x(B, color) . True example: both are red. Counterexample: A is red and B is blue. Two suspects have different values ¶ Type: suspect_different_from . Suspects "A" and "B" have different "color" values. Formal: x(A, color) ≠ x(B, color) . True example: A is red and B is blue. Counterexample: both are red. Someone has both properties ¶ Type: indirect_positive . At least one suspect has "color" = "red" and "room" = "hall". Formal: there exists an s with x(s, color) = red and x(s, room) = hall . True example: A is red and in the hall. Counterexample: A is red/in the study; B is blue/in the hall. The same suspect must satisfy both halves. The clue does not identify that suspect as the culprit. Nobody has both properties ¶ Type: indirect_negative . No suspect has both "color" = "red" and "room" = "hall". Formal: no s has both x(s, color) = red and x(s, room) = hall . True example: A is red/in the study; B is blue/in the hall. Counterexample: A is red/in the hall. Red by itself is allowed. Being in the hall by itself is allowed. Only their combination is forbidden. An unrelated record has a value ¶ Type: record_positive . Record COMPONENT: its independent value equals "0". Formal: y(COMPONENT, value) = 0 , with declared domain {0, 1} and no target variables. True example: the component's value is 0. Counterexample: its value is 1. Each generated component has one in-domain assertion, so the stream is satisfiable and leaves target candidates unchanged. It is not an entailed fact about suspects or culprit attributes.

docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ Start with the message you received. An incomplete or unresolved result is reported explicitly; it is never silently treated as a certified puzzle. When generation cannot finish ¶ Candidate exhaustion ¶ Inspect the saved rejection reasons. Use a fresh output directory with a revised configuration. Increasing a retry limit cannot make contradictory requirements feasible. An incomplete bank uses exit status 2 . Solver timeout or work exhaustion ¶ The result is unresolved . Use a declared larger offline budget on fresh outputs if appropriate. Do not disable certification or count the timeout as a proof. Distinct values exhausted ¶ Expand the domains or active-value set, or reduce the number of suspects. Equality construction families require repeated assignments. Family and enabled types disagree ¶ Restore the required predicates or choose a compatible family and route. redundant_paths needs exactly suspect_count + 1 reports per attribute. Impossible quotas or coalition requirements ¶ Check the shared count, replication factor and per-agent quotas. Coalition checks support at most eight agents . More retries do not fix impossible quotas. Ambiguity conflicts with a sufficient subset ¶ For globally ambiguous cases, set the sufficient bounds and minimum coalition size to null . Do not claim a unique answer. When outputs already exist ¶ Exports, reports and replays need a fresh destination: clue-benchmark examples replay nuisance-followup \ --output runs/nuisance-new Generation can resume a checkpoint only when the source and configuration match. Complete matching datasets return without being rewritten. For a stale schema, source or configuration, use the frozen historical source for its historical plan—or prepare a new plan and output. Do not rewrite hashes to make an old plan pass. When size bounds cannot be met ¶ Tokenizer is absent ¶ Supply a tokenizer with a stable identity through Python and use workers=1 , or remove token constraints. Do not silently substitute another tokenizer. Word or token bounds are impossible ¶ Raise the bound or explicitly change the requested evidence. The generator never truncates evidence to fit. Model context would overflow ¶ Reject the request before dispatch. Do not omit evidence or shrink an answer allowance after freezing a matched study. When a model run fails ¶ Keep failure types separate A wrong answer, malformed final action, provider failure and unresolved budget hold are different outcomes. Malformed tool call or missing final action ¶ Retain a protocol failure. Inspect the saved finish reason separately from reasoning errors. Provider error, model drift or unknown usage ¶ Stop and preserve the returned identity, safe receipt and maximum reservation. Reconcile from documented evidence; do not edit ledger balances or assume zero cost. Held funds after an interruption ¶ Resume only with the same plan, sources and durable ledger. An unresolved dispatch must not replay automatically. Zero automatic retries is intentional. Supported platforms ¶ Python: 3.12–3.14 checked on Linux and macOS in hosted CI. Local installation: clean offline candidate-wheel checks on macOS Python 3.12–3.14; source-archive installation also checked. Windows: not advertised as verified. Generation and saved-data replay are distinct from optional native provider paths. Check PR #2 for checks on the current revision.

docs.text: Results at a glance ¶ The surprising pilot result did not repeat consistently: extra irrelevant evidence cost much more, without a reliable accuracy benefit in the follow-up. Scored responses 144 Plus two compatibility probes. Underlying worlds 12 Six per evidence-burden setting. Estimated total $6.96 Under the single $10.00 cap. Jump to original studies and downloads · Read the open questions What we learned ¶ The earlier improvement was fragile ¶ In the original pilot, Lite improved from 2/5 to 5/5 between zero and 1,000 irrelevant records. In the expanded follow-up's four-report setting, it scored 10/12 at both endpoints . An unchanged average hid individual changes ¶ Four primary worlds stayed unchanged. One improved and one worsened. docs.text: What is still unanswered? ¶ The preview is public. The research findings are preliminary, and the full licensed release still has unfinished reviews. Research questions ¶ Does irrelevant evidence ever help consistently? ¶ The original five-world Lite improvement did not repeat in the expanded follow-up. The primary change was zero, with a descriptive interval of −25 to +25 percentage points on six worlds. What would help: a larger, separately preregistered fresh sample that distinguishes a repeatable benefit from sampling and response variation. Why did individual worlds change? ¶ Four primary worlds stayed unchanged, one improved and one worsened. Those outcomes do not identify a reasoning mechanism. What would help: separate controls for content, report order and context length before attributing the changes to distraction or useful extra computation. Is the harder-setting dip repeatable? ¶ Lite's 9/12 → 5/12 → 7/12 pattern is small and non-monotonic. What would help: fresh matched worlds and a better estimate of ordinary response variation. When is extra context worth the cost? ¶ In the four-report setting, costs rose roughly 56× for Lite and 77× for Flash without higher endpoint accuracy. What would help: comparisons involving useful redundancy, related distractors, different models and explicit resource allowances. What makes a puzzle difficult? ¶ Minimum necessary evidence measures information burden, not proof depth or model difficulty. What would help: structural predictors of errors that control for construction heuristics, input length and output budget. How stable are results across model and budget changes? ¶ The adaptive six-world output-budget comparison and fresh 48-world confirmation answer different questions. What would help: fresh matched comparisons before generalizing across thinking budgets, output allowances, input formats or model revisions. Can agents learn useful communication? ¶ Current star forwarding is programmed. It demonstrates evidence delivery, not learned collaboration or an efficient communication policy. What would help: an explicitly different experiment measuring what agents choose to send and whether those choices deliver sufficient evidence. Do completion and supported correctness improve together? ¶ Qwen's matched returned slots showed more completed actions without higher supported correctness. docs.text: Your first dataset ¶ Generate a small puzzle, check it, and give an agent only the evidence it is allowed to see. You need: Python 3.12 or newer on macOS or Linux. Installation downloads dependencies; every exercise below then runs offline. No model account or API key is required. 1. Install the preview ¶ Clone the published candidate, then enter its directory: git clone \ --branch v0.5.0rc2 \ --single-branch \ https://github.com/TrustPrism/clue-benchmark.git cd clue-benchmark Create an isolated Python environment and install the package: python3 -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate python -m pip install . Already have a built candidate wheel? Install that file instead: python -m pip install \ /path/to/trustprism_clue_benchmark-0.5.0rc2-py3-none-any.whl The package is not published to PyPI. Licensing remains pending; installation instructions do not grant redistribution rights. 2. Generate a puzzle ¶ clue-benchmark generate-dataset \ --preset quickstart \ --output runs/demo The preset asks for one single-agent case with exactly four necessary reports . Look for complete: true in the JSON summary. runs/demo is relative to your current directory. You can run the installed command from anywhere. If generation stops early Generation uses bounded search. An incomplete result means it did not find enough certified cases within that budget. It never substitutes an uncertified puzzle. See candidate exhaustion . 3. Validate it ¶ clue-benchmark validate-dataset runs/demo Expected: status: verified . This checks both the bundle and the puzzle's logical meaning. 4. Export the agent's evidence ¶ clue-benchmark export-public runs/demo \ --agent 0 \ --output runs/agent.jsonl Give your agent runs/agent.jsonl , not the whole runs/demo directory. The exported file contains public case and report rows. The original directory also contains evaluator answers and certificates. The export leaves out solutions, checkpoints, provider receipts and other private fields. Inspect the public view: clue-benchmark inspect-case runs/demo --agent 0 5. Score a sample agent ¶ This intentionally cautious agent always abstains: from clue_benchmark import evaluate_agent result = evaluate_agent( "runs/demo", lambda observation: {"kind": "abstain"}, output="runs/sample-score.json", agent_id=0, ) print(result["episodes"][0]) Its response is valid , but abstaining is unnecessary when the evidence identifies an answer. Valid format and successful reasoning are different scores. See all score meanings . 6. Open a readable report ¶ clue-benchmark report runs/sample-score.json \ --output runs/sample-report Open runs/sample-report/index.html in your browser. The report also links the exact saved JSON. It makes no model calls. Try the measured example ¶ Replay the completed irrelevant-evidence study from saved measurements: clue-benchmark examples replay nuisance-followup \ --output runs/followup The output separates the initial study , final expansion and exploratory combined result . It includes all 144 scored assignments and the closed $10.00 study accounting. Read what the study found → Explore the settings ¶ See the available presets: clue-benchmark presets list Inspect the quickstart's resolved settings: clue-benchmark presets show quickstart clue-benchmark explain-config --preset quickstart Start with worked research recipes , then use the parameter reference for details. Existing files, checkpoints and resuming Generation can resume a matching checkpoint with the same source and configuration. Exports, reports and replays need a new destination. They refuse to overwrite an existing one. A changed source or configuration needs a new generation directory. Do not edit frozen measured runs or ledgers to bypass an error. docs.text: clue-benchmark export-public runs/demo \ --agent 0 \ --output runs/agent.jsonl Give your agent runs/agent.jsonl , not the whole runs/demo directory. The exported file contains public case and report rows. The original directory also contains evaluator answers and certificates. The export leaves out solutions, checkpoints, provider receipts and other private fields. Inspect the public view: clue-benchmark inspect-case runs/demo --agent 0
docs.title: 4. Export the agent's evidence

docs.text: This intentionally cautious agent always abstains: from clue_benchmark import evaluate_agent result = evaluate_agent( "runs/demo", lambda observation: {"kind": "abstain"}, output="runs/sample-score.json", agent_id=0, ) print(result["episodes"][0]) Its response is valid , but abstaining is unnecessary when the evidence identifies an answer. Valid format and successful reasoning are different scores. See all score meanings .
docs.title: 5. Score a sample agent

docs.text: clue-benchmark report runs/sample-score.json \ --output runs/sample-report Open runs/sample-report/index.html in your browser. The report also links the exact saved JSON. It makes no model calls.
docs.title: 6. Open a readable report

docs.text: Replay the completed irrelevant-evidence study from saved measurements: clue-benchmark examples replay nuisance-followup \ --output runs/followup The output separates the initial study , final expansion and exploratory combined result . It includes all 144 scored assignments and the closed $10.00 study accounting. Read what the study found →
docs.title: Try the measured example

docs.text: See the available presets: clue-benchmark presets list Inspect the quickstart's resolved settings: clue-benchmark presets show quickstart clue-benchmark explain-config --preset quickstart Start with worked research recipes , then use the parameter reference for details. Existing files, checkpoints and resuming Generation can resume a matching checkpoint with the same source and configuration. Exports, reports and replays need a new destination. They refuse to overwrite an existing one. A changed source or configuration needs a new generation directory. Do not edit frozen measured runs or ledgers to bypass an error. The data dictionary describes the five bundle files.
